CREATE TABLE `actions`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `class_name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `username` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `information` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `description` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `cache`(
    `key` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `value` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `expiration` INT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE `component_groups`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `order` INT NOT NULL,
    `visible` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `collapsed` INT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);


CREATE TABLE `components`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `description` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `link` TEXT NULL,
    `status` INT NOT NULL,
    `order` INT NOT NULL,
    `group_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `enabled` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `meta` LONGTEXT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `deleted_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`group_id`) REFERENCES `component_groups`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`)
);




CREATE TABLE `failed_jobs`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `connection` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `queue` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `payload` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `failed_at` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `incident_components`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `incident_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `component_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `status_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`component_id`) REFERENCES `components`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`incident_id`) REFERENCES `incidents`(`id`)
);



CREATE TABLE `incident_templates`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `slug` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `template` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `deleted_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `incident_updates`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `incident_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `status` INT NOT NULL,
    `message` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`incident_id`) REFERENCES `incidents`(`id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `incidents`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `user_id` INT NULL,
    `component_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `status` INT NOT NULL,
    `visible` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `stickied` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `notifications` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `message` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `occurred_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `deleted_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`component_id`) REFERENCES `components`(`id`)
);





CREATE TABLE `invites`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `code` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `email` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `claimed_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);

CREATE TABLE `jobs`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `queue` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `payload` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `attempts` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `reserved` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `reserved_at` INT NULL,
    `available_at` INT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` INT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `meta`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `key` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `value` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `meta_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `meta_type` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);


CREATE TABLE `metric_points`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `metric_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `value` DECIMAL(8, 2) NOT NULL,
    `counter` INT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`metric_id`) REFERENCES `metrics`(`id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `metrics`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `suffix` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `description` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `default_value` DECIMAL(8, 2) NOT NULL,
    `calc_type` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `display_chart` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `places` INT NOT NULL,
    `default_view` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `threshold` INT NOT NULL,
    `order` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `visible` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);


CREATE TABLE `notifications`(
    `id` CHAR(255) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `type` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `notifiable_type` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `notifiable_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `data` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `read_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`notifiable_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`notifiable_id`) REFERENCES `subscribers`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`notifiable_id`) REFERENCES `invites`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `schedule_components`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `schedule_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `component_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `component_status` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`component_id`) REFERENCES `components`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`schedule_id`) REFERENCES `schedules`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `schedules`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `message` LONGTEXT NULL,
    `status` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `scheduled_at` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    `completed_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `deleted_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `sessions`(
    `id` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NULL,
    `ip_address` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `user_agent` TEXT NULL,
    `payload` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `last_activity` INT NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `settings`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `value` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `subscribers`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `email` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `verify_code` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `phone_number` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `slack_webhook_url` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `verified_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `global` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);

CREATE TABLE `subscriptions`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `subscriber_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `component_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`component_id`) REFERENCES `components`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`subscriber_id`) REFERENCES `subscribers`(`id`)
);


CREATE TABLE `taggables`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `tag_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `taggable_type` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `taggable_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`tag_id`) REFERENCES `tags`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`taggable_id`) REFERENCES `incidents`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`taggable_id`) REFERENCES `components`(`id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `tags`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `slug` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);

CREATE TABLE `users`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `username` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `password` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `remember_token` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `google_2fa_secret` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `email` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `api_key` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `active` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `level` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `welcomed` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);

Background / Context

Cachet is an open-source, self-hosted status page system built using Laravel. It is designed to enhance communication regarding system statuses, particularly for applications experiencing downtime, maintenance, or outages. The system is responsive, ensuring consistent performance across various devices, and is suitable for businesses and organizations of all sizes. Status pages are a critical component of an organization's communication strategy, helping keep users, teams, and stakeholders informed during incidents.

 Objectives

The primary objective of Cachet is to provide a platform that enables organizations to effectively communicate system statuses to their users and stakeholders. This includes communicating ongoing and resolved incidents, scheduled maintenance, and general system performance updates. The aim is to promote transparency and trust between the organization and its user base.

 Stakeholders & Users

- Businesses and Organizations: Any size organization looking to maintain transparency with users.
- System Administrators: Individuals who manage the status pages and update system information.
- End Users: Customers, teams, shareholders, and other stakeholders relying on system status information.

 Functional Descriptions

1. Status Communication:
   - Display current system status and historical data.
   - Notify users of incidents and maintenance schedules.
   - Provide detailed descriptions and updates on incidents and components.
   
2. Incident Management:
   - Create, update, and manage incidents.
   - Associate incidents with specific components.
   - Use incident templates for efficient reporting.

3. Component Management:
   - Organize services into components and component groups.
   - Track and display component status.

4. Subscriber Management:
   - Users can subscribe to status updates via email or Slack.
   - Manage subscriber information and notification preferences.

5. Metrics and Analytics:
   - Define metrics to track performance.
   - Display metrics with charts and set thresholds for alerts.

6. Notification System:
   - Configure notifications for various user preferences.
   - Manage and store notifications with timestamps and read status.

 Non-Functional Descriptions

- Scalability: Support a growing number of users and components without degradation in performance.
- Security: Ensure data protection and secure handling of user information and API keys.
- Usability: Provide an intuitive user interface that is easy for administrators and users to navigate.
- Customization: Allow customization of the status page interface and notification settings to fit organizational needs.
- Responsiveness: Deliver consistent and optimal performance across desktops, tablets, and mobile devices.
nl_text: The schemabench_0010 database is a comprehensive system for managing various aspects of a complex application, including user management, incident tracking, and scheduling. At its core, the database contains 24 tables that work together to store and retrieve data. The users table holds information about each registered user, including their username, password, email, and API key, with fields for tracking their activity status, level, and welcome status. The incidents table stores details about reported incidents, such as their name, status, and associated component, while the components table contains information about the components involved in these incidents, including their name, description, and status. The incident_updates table tracks updates made to incidents, including the user who made the update and the new status. The incident_components table links incidents to their associated components, and the taggables table allows for the assignment of tags to both incidents and components. The tags table stores the actual tags used, with fields for their name and slug. The subscribers table manages user subscriptions, including their email, phone number, and Slack webhook URL, while the subscriptions table links subscribers to the components they are subscribed to. The notifications table stores notifications sent to users, including the type of notification, the notifiable item, and the data associated with it. The settings table holds application-wide settings, such as the default value for metrics. The metrics table stores information about the metrics being tracked, including their name, suffix, and description, while the metric_points table stores the actual metric values. The cache table stores cached data, with fields for the key, value, and expiration time. The jobs table manages background jobs, including their queue, payload, and status. The failed_jobs table tracks failed jobs, including the connection, queue, and payload. The sessions table stores user session information, including the user ID, IP address, and user agent. The schedule_components table links components to their associated schedules, and the schedules table stores the actual schedules, including their name, message, and status. The invites table manages user invitations, including the invitation code, email, and claimed status. The meta table stores metadata about the application, including key-value pairs. The notifications table has a unique primary key, and the cache table has a unique key and value. The schemabench_0010 database also includes several foreign key constraints to ensure data consistency and integrity, such as linking users to incidents, components, and subscribers, as well as linking components to groups and schedules.
